issues.description: Command name mismatch: code registers `quickmarks_reload`/`bookmarks_reload` but feature tests invoke `:quickmarks-reload`/`:bookmarks-reload` which won't resolve
issues.detail: The new methods are `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` (plural marks + reload). Qutebrowser's @cmdutils.register converts underscores to dashes, producing `:quickmarks-reload` and `:bookmarks-reload`. However, every other quickmark/bookmark command in the file uses the singular `quickmark_*`/`bookmark_*` form (e.g. `quickmark_save`, `bookmark_add`, `bookmark_load`). This naming is inconsistent with the rest of the command surface and likely intentionally diverges from the project's naming convention. The maintainers will almost certainly ask for `:quickmark-reload` / `:bookmark-reload` to match the existing namespace.

issues.description: `reload()` does not handle the case where the marks file has been deleted or fails to parse
issues.detail: `reload()` calls `self.marks.clear()` first, then re-reads the file via `_init_lineparser`. If `_init_lineparser` or `_parse_line` raises (e.g. `ParseError`, `DoesNotExistError`), the manager is left in an empty, inconsistent state with `changed` not emitted. The original `__init__` path could tolerate this because the object was being constructed, but at runtime reload this silently wipes user data. Wrap reload in a try/except that restores the previous `marks` on failure, or at least surface the error via `message.error` and preserve prior state.

issues.description: Reload bypasses save-manager dirty-state semantics and may race with autosave
issues.detail: `UrlMarkManager` registers with the save-manager (`_init_savemanager`) which periodically writes `self.marks` to disk. Calling `reload()` clears and repopulates `self.marks` without coordinating with the save-manager; if an autosave fires between `marks.clear()` and the file being fully re-parsed, the on-disk file can be overwritten with an empty/partial mark set. The `changed` signal also marks the manager as dirty in normal code paths, so emitting it post-reload may schedule an unnecessary save that re-serializes whatever was just read. Either suppress save-on-reload or explicitly snapshot/restore the save-manager dirty flag.

issues.description: Missing `Closes #NNNN` link / no issue reference, and no changelog/doc update
issues.detail: qutebrowser typically requires user-facing command additions to update `doc/help/commands.asciidoc` (auto-generated but committed) and `doc/changelog.asciidoc`. Neither is touched here. Without doc regen, `:help :quickmarks-reload` will not work and the changelog will miss the feature. Also, the PR description lacks a `Closes #NNNN` / issue reference per the PR template note.

Both new Gherkin scenarios are declared as `Scenario:` with no title. Other scenarios in this feature file all have descriptive names (e.g. `Scenario: Saving a quickmark (:quickmark-add)`). Unnamed scenarios produce poor test output and break the project's convention. Give them titles like `Scenario: Reloading bookmarks (:bookmark-reload)`.

issues.description: Unit test does not verify that the LineParser actually picks up the new file contents
issues.detail: `test_reload` rewrites `bm_file` after `BookmarkManager()` is constructed and then calls `bm.reload()`. The LineParser instance was created during `__init__`; `_init_lineparser` is called again inside `reload()`, but whether it re-reads from disk depends on `LineParser` semantics. The test passing relies on that implementation detail without asserting it. Add a comment or assert on the intermediate state (e.g. assert pre-reload marks match the first write) to make the regression target explicit.

issues.description: `__init__` no longer emits `changed` only once at startup — now emits via reload()
issues.detail: Previously `__init__` populated `self.marks` without emitting `changed`. After the refactor, `reload()` (called from `__init__`) ends with `self.changed.emit()`. Any slot connected before construction completes (none today, but a behavior change) will now fire on initial load. Likely harmless but worth a one-line note in the commit message or a defensive `if not initial:` flag.

issues.description: Extra blank line after `quickmark_manager.reload()` / `bookmark_manager.reload()` is stylistically inconsistent
issues.detail: Adjacent command methods in `commands.py` do not have a blank line between the body and the trailing `message.info(...)` call. Trivial nit but worth aligning with surrounding style.

issues.description: No type annotation on new `reload()` method
issues.detail: `urlmarks.py` annotates `self.marks: MutableMapping[str, str]` and other modern code in the file uses typing. `reload()` should be annotated `-> None:` for consistency with the codebase's typing posture.

issues.description: Command does no-op feedback distinction (e.g. count delta)
issues.detail: The user gets `Quickmarks reloaded.` regardless of whether 0 or 500 entries loaded, or whether the file was unreadable. A small UX improvement: include the count, e.g. `Quickmarks reloaded (42 entries).`, matching the helpfulness of other qutebrowser status messages.

dissents.topic: Whether reload() should preserve previous marks on parse failure

positions.position: reload() must be transactional: parse into a temp dict first, then atomically swap. Otherwise a malformed line can wipe a user's quickmarks at runtime with no recovery.

The existing __init__ path already had the same behavior; reload simply reuses it. Keeping the behavior identical is the conservative refactor. Add transactional swap as a follow-up rather than expanding scope of a small feature PR.
Every existing command is singular (`quickmark-add`, `quickmark-save`, `bookmark-add`, `bookmark-load`). New commands must follow suit: `:quickmark-reload`, `:bookmark-reload`.
Reloading is a collection-level operation, not a per-mark one, so plural reads more naturally and signals scope. The argument has merit but project conventions usually win in code review.

dissents.topic: Whether to expose reload as a command at all, or rely on a file-watcher

positions.position: An explicit command is simple, debuggable, and matches qutebrowser's keyboard-driven UX. Ship it.
If users want fresh data after editing the file, a QFileSystemWatcher on the marks file would auto-reload and eliminate the need for the command. The command is a workaround for a missing capability.

review.summary: The PR adds two small commands (`:quickmarks-reload`, `:bookmarks-reload`) and refactors `UrlMarkManager` to expose a `reload()` method, with reasonable test coverage. The core refactor is clean and the unit test is well-shaped. However, the command names diverge from the project's established singular convention (`quickmark-*`, `bookmark-*`), which is a likely-blocking review nit. More substantively, `reload()` clears `self.marks` before re-parsing with no error handling, so any parse failure or transient I/O issue silently wipes the user's marks at runtime — a regression risk the original __init__-only path never had to worry about. The feature-test scenarios are unnamed (breaking file conventions), and standard qutebrowser PR hygiene (changelog, doc regen, `Closes #...`) is missing. Recommend addressing the naming, adding transactional/error-safe reload, and tightening tests before merge.
